hero.title: Giving robusta a reason to be chosen
hero.intro: Robarica is a Wellington brand selling Vietnamese robusta coffee, grown in the Central Highlands of Vietnam and sold mainly on Amazon in the US. Working with the founder, I refreshed its main coffee pouch, designed the packaging for a new instant coffee, made its marketing images and designed the cover of its brewing guide.

image.alt: The Robarica Coffee of Vietnam pouch lying on a white desk next to a cup of black coffee

p: Robarica sells 100% Vietnamese robusta: dark roasted, low in acidity and naturally high in caffeine. Most people know robusta, if they know it at all, as the cheap filler in instant coffee, and that reputation was the main thing standing between the product and a new customer.

Robarica already had a pouch, built around the brand's botanical artwork and a serif title. My job was to refresh it so that robusta comes across as a bold, distinctive coffee with [[a character of its own]], next to arabica brands that have never had to explain themselves.

blocks.text: The packaging needed to treat robusta as a coffee worth choosing, not a cheaper substitute.

blocks.alt: Two Robarica pouches side by side: the previous design with a serif Coffee of Vietnam title, and the refreshed design with a wide Coffee of Vietnam title
blocks.caption: The previous pouch with its serif title on the left, and the refreshed design on the right.

sections.heading: Proud of where it comes from

blocks.title: Vietnam on the front
p: The new front leads with the origin: Coffee of Vietnam, set large in a wide typeface, with the star from the Vietnamese flag in the middle of the name.

The border of coffee leaves, cherries, flowers and star anise is the brand's own artwork, so I kept it as the frame and gave the type a dark panel of its own. That makes [[the origin the first thing people read]], before the product details.

image.alt: The Robarica logo above Coffee of Viet Nam, with a star between Viet and Nam, framed by painted coffee leaves and cherries
image.caption: The origin became the headline, inside the brand's existing botanical border.

blocks.title: One frame, two products
p: The new instant 3-in-1 coffee uses the same frame, logo and type as the whole bean pouch, with only the product name changing. That keeps the two products [[clearly part of one family]], and it gives Robarica a layout it can reuse for future products.

image.alt: The front artwork of the whole bean pouch and the smaller instant coffee pack, side by side on black
image.caption: The whole bean pouch and the new instant coffee share one layout.

blocks.title: The back of the pack teaches
p: Robusta behaves differently from the coffee most people are used to, so the back of the pack is [[a short brewing guide]] rather than a block of marketing copy.
It has numbered steps for a Vietnamese phin filter and an espresso machine, with simple icons, and a QR code that leads to the full brewing guide.

image.alt: The back of the pouch: Make a perfect cup of coffee, with numbered steps for a Vietnamese phin filter and an espresso machine
image.caption: Brewing steps for a phin and an espresso machine, with a QR code to the free guide further down.

sections.heading: The first look is a product page

p: Robarica sells mainly on Amazon, so for many people the marketing images are their first look at the coffee, long before they hold the pouch.

One image explains the pack itself, with its zip, one-way valve and protective inner layer. The others repeat the points that matter most for robusta, [[100% pure and 100% Vietnamese]], strong and aromatic, and pair the coffee with the people and places it comes from.

p: Robusta can be unforgiving when it is brewed casually, and a harsh first cup can easily turn into a bad review. The ebook, How to Make a Perfect Cup of Coffee, was designed as a practical brewing guide: part education, part product support, and part confidence for first-time customers.
